title: When to visit Kashmir: seasons, roads and snow
meta_description: When to visit Kashmir: month-by-month weather, which roads and passes are open, tulip and saffron weeks, Amarnath crowds, Gulmarg snow and altitude tips.
summary: April to June and September to October are the easiest months for Kashmir, with green meadows or clear autumn skies. January to March is for snow and skiing in Gulmarg. July and August bring the Amarnath Yatra. High roads to Gurez and Zoji La open only from about May or June to November.

sections.heading: Kashmir's four seasons in short
paras: The Kashmir valley floor sits near 1,600 m and is ringed by mountains, so it has four clear seasons rather than a monsoon. Kashmiris name them sonth for spring, grishm for summer, harud for autumn and wandh for winter. Each changes what you can do, which roads are open and what you pay.

Spring, from March to May, brings almond blossom, then tulips, then fresh green on the meadows, with some rain. Summer, June to August, is warm in Srinagar and pleasant in the hills, with afternoon showers and the Amarnath pilgrimage. Autumn, September to November, is dry and clear, with chinars turning red and saffron in flower. Winter, December to February, is cold, with snow in Gulmarg and on the hills and the lakes freezing at the edges in the coldest weeks.

sections.heading: Month by month at a glance
paras: The table uses typical Srinagar temperatures. Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg are 6–10 °C cooler, and Gurez is cooler still at night. Weather varies year to year.

Ratings in our planning follow the same pattern: September, October, April, May and June are our top months for a first trip; January and February are top months only if snow is the point of the journey. March, July, August, November and December all work well with the right plan and a little flexibility.

sections.heading: Spring: blossom, tulips and green meadows
paras: Spring starts with almond blossom in the old Badamwari garden below Hari Parbat in March, weather permitting. The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden on the Zabarwan slopes usually opens in late March or early April for three to four weeks; the Floriculture Department announces dates each year, and bloom depends on temperature. Weekdays at opening time are far quieter than weekend afternoons.

By May the meadows of Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Doodhpathri and Yusmarg are green and the peaks still carry snow. This is the most popular time with Indian families, and also the most expensive. Book rooms, flights and gondola slots weeks ahead, and plan meadow day trips for weekdays, because Srinagar families fill Doodhpathri and Yusmarg on Sundays.

Spring weather is changeable. A warm week can be followed by two days of rain and fresh snow on the hills, and Gondola Phase 2 at Apharwat often stays closed or snowbound into April. Pack a rain shell and a warm layer even in May, and keep one flexible day for the meadows. The Kheer Bhawani mela at Tulmulla, on Jyeshtha Ashtami in May or June, draws Kashmiri Pandit families from across India and is worth timing a trip around.

sections.heading: Summer and the Amarnath Yatra
paras: June to August is the season for high ground. The road over the Razdan Pass to Gurez is usually open from about late May, and treks such as the Kashmir Great Lakes route from Sonamarg run from about July to September. Srinagar can reach the low 30s °C in the afternoon, so plan city sights for mornings and evenings.

The Amarnath Yatra runs in July and August, in the Hindu month of Shravan, from base camps at Pahalgam and Baltal near Sonamarg. Hundreds of thousands of registered pilgrims travel, and security is heavy. For other travellers it means convoy timings on the Pahalgam and Sonamarg roads, full hotels in those towns and, at times, restricted access to Chandanwari and nearby meadows. Srinagar, Gulmarg and Gurez are much less affected. Check current status before you travel.

Summer rain comes as short afternoon showers rather than a monsoon, but heavy spells do cause landslides on the Jammu highway and on mountain roads. July and August are also the months when Srinagar is busiest with traffic, so plan Mughal garden visits at opening time and keep the boulevard for the evening.

sections.heading: Autumn: the clearest season
paras: September and October are the steadiest months in the valley. Rain is rare, the air is clear, and every road is normally open, including Gurez and Zoji La. It is our first choice for most travellers, and prices sit at shoulder-season levels.

From late October the chinars turn red and copper in the Mughal gardens and along the Jhelum, and the saffron crocus flowers on the karewas around Pampore, usually for about three weeks from the last week of October. Nights get cold quickly: by November, Srinagar mornings are near freezing and the first snow often dusts the high peaks. Some guesthouses in Aru, Sonamarg and Gurez close by mid-November, and the Gurez road shuts with the first heavy snow.

Autumn is also harvest time. Paddy is cut and stacked in the fields in September and October, apples are picked and packed in the orchards of the south and north of the valley, and families dry vegetables on their roofs for winter. Roads past the orchards around Sopore and Shopian are lined with fruit trucks heading for the plains.

sections.heading: Winter: snow, Gulmarg and Chillai Kalan
paras: Winter is for snow. Gulmarg usually has skiable snow from late December or early January to March, and its gondola and slopes draw skiers from India and abroad. Sonamarg and Pahalgam take snow too, and day trips are possible when roads are cleared. The Sonamarg tunnel at Z-Morh, opened in early 2025, keeps that road open beyond its old winter limit, subject to snow clearance.

The coldest stretch is Chillai Kalan, the 40 days from about 21 December to late January. People wear the long woollen pheran and carry a kangri, a wicker-wrapped clay pot of embers, beneath it. Harissa, slow-cooked mutton and rice, is sold in old-city shops at dawn. Snow and fog can close the Jammu–Srinagar highway and delay flights for a day or more, so keep buffer days.

Winter has quiet rewards beyond Gulmarg. Srinagar has few visitors, hotels and houseboats are cheap, and the Mughal gardens and Dal Lake under snow are rarely crowded. Power cuts are more frequent, so choose rooms with backup heating and ask about it before booking.

sections.heading: Roads, passes and altitude
paras: Most of Kashmir's tourist places sit between 1,585 m and 2,750 m, where altitude is rarely a problem for healthy travellers. The exceptions are Gondola Phase 2 at Apharwat, near 3,950 m, the Razdan Pass on the way to Gurez at about 3,300 m, and Zoji La at about 3,528 m. You only pass through these, but walk slowly at the top, drink water and come down if you feel unwell. If you have heart or lung conditions, talk to your doctor before travelling.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Kashmir?
faqs.a: September is our first choice: dry, clear, every road open and shoulder-season prices. April to June is best for green meadows and the tulip garden but busy and costly. October and early November add chinar colour and saffron. Choose January or February for snow and skiing in Gulmarg.

faqs.q: When does the Srinagar tulip garden open?
faqs.a: Usually in late March or early April, for about three to four weeks, depending on temperature. The Floriculture Department announces dates each year. Visit on a weekday at opening time to avoid crowds. Check the official announcement before fixing travel dates, as a cold spring can push the bloom later.

faqs.q: When can I see snow in Kashmir?
faqs.a: Gulmarg usually has snow from December to March, with the most reliable cover in January and February. Sonamarg and Pahalgam also get winter snow. Gondola Phase 2 at Apharwat may hold snow into April or May. In summer you can see old snow at Thajiwas near Sonamarg and on high passes.

faqs.q: Is it a good idea to visit Kashmir in July or August?
faqs.a: Yes, with planning. Weather is warm, meadows are green, and Gurez and the high treks are open. The Amarnath Yatra brings convoys and full hotels to Pahalgam and Sonamarg, and access to some areas may be restricted. Base yourself in Srinagar and Gulmarg, or visit Gurez, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How cold is Kashmir in December and January?
faqs.a: Srinagar ranges from about −3 °C at night to 6–8 °C by day, with freezing fog on some mornings. Gulmarg falls to −10 °C or lower at night. Hotels have heaters, but power cuts happen. Pack thermal layers, a down jacket, warm boots, gloves and a hat.

faqs.q: When is the road to Gurez open?
faqs.a: Usually from about late May to November, when snow on the Razdan Pass closes it. June to early October is the safest window. Opening depends on snow clearance and can shift by weeks. Indians register with ID at checkposts; foreigners have needed prior permission. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When does saffron flower in Pampore?
faqs.a: Usually from the last week of October to the middle of November, peaking for about two weeks. Families pick the flowers at dawn. Dates shift with weather, so keep a few days flexible and ask locally before going. Pampore is about 15 km from Srinagar, an easy morning trip.

faqs.q: Will altitude sickness affect me in Kashmir?
faqs.a: Rarely, on most trips. Srinagar is at 1,585 m and Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg are between 2,200 m and 2,750 m. Short visits to Gondola Phase 2 near 3,950 m or the Razdan Pass at about 3,300 m can bring headache or breathlessness; go slowly and come down if unwell. Talk to your doctor if you have heart or lung conditions.

faqs.q: Which months are cheapest for a Kashmir trip?
faqs.a: November, March and early December outside the holidays are cheapest, followed by July and August in Srinagar and Gulmarg. Houseboats and hotels negotiate more in these months. Late April, May, June and holiday weeks such as Diwali and Christmas to New Year are the most expensive.
